claims.claim: Brown bullheads did not feed at all in a 2 °C Connecticut pond (Massengill 1973, via Ellman 2023)
claims.note: full text not obtained. The abstract (not used to confirm) says bullheads overwintering in the heated discharge canal of the Connecticut Yankee Atomic Power Company plant fed, while those 'in water at 2 C' from Chapman Pond 'did not'; it calls Chapman Pond 'a cove of the Connecticut River unaffected by artificial heating' — so 'a Connecticut pond' should be 'a cove of the Connecticut River (Chapman Pond)'. The sample sizes, dates and the meaning of 'did not' (empty stomachs?) need the full text

claims.claim: all × 0.7, buried and fasting below ~8 °C (no feeding at 2 °C, Massengill 1973)
claims.note: as above. The abstract's last visible words are 'Bullheads began feeding before the temperature reached 4' (cut off), which suggests feeding resumed at about 4 °C in the canal or in spring — a lower threshold than the code's ~8 °C, if the full text bears it out. Nothing in the abstract on burying
